title: Toxicity Is a Property of Communicative Events: A Contextual Stress Measurement Framework for NLP
abstract: arXiv:2503.16072v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Toxicity detection has become core safety infrastructure for online moderation, dataset filtering, and deployed language-model systems. Yet most detectors still treat toxicity as an intrinsic property of isolated text. This position paper argues that toxicity detection should be evaluated as the contextual measurement of situated communicative harm, rather than as single-label text classification. Toxicity is not contained in words alone; it emerges when a communicative act is interpreted by an audience within a normative and social context.   We introduce the Contextual Stress Framework (CSF), which defines toxicity as a relation between perceived norm violation and induced stress or disruption. CSF explains why text-intrinsic detectors overflag dialectal or reclaimed language, miss coded or pragmatic abuse, and remain brittle under meaning-preserving transformations.

translated_title: 毒性是传播事件的属性：面向自然语言处理的语境压力测量框架
translated_abstract: 毒性检测已成为在线内容审核、数据集过滤和已部署语言模型系统的核心安全基础设施。然而，大多数检测器仍将毒性视为孤立文本的内在属性。这篇立场论文认为，毒性检测应被评估为对特定情境下传播伤害的语境化测量，而非单标签文本分类。毒性并非仅蕴含于词语之中；当传播行为在规范和社会语境中被受众解读时，毒性才会显现。我们提出了语境压力框架（CSF），将毒性定义为被感知的规范违反与所引发的压力或干扰之间的关系。CSF解释了为什么基于文本内在属性的检测器会对方言或语义回收的语言过度标记，遗漏隐语或语用层面的滥用，并且在保持语义的转换下依然表现脆弱。
tldr: 论文提出语境压力框架（CSF），主张毒性应被视为在特定社会与规范语境下由传播行为引发的伤害，而非文本的内在属性，从而解释了现有文本检测器过度标记方言、遗漏隐晦滥用等问题。
en_tdlr: This position paper proposes the Contextual Stress Framework (CSF), arguing that toxicity should be measured as situated communicative harm within normative and social contexts rather than as an intrinsic property of isolated text, explaining why text-intrinsic detectors overflag dialectal language and miss coded or pragmatic abuse.
